benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official points: Sagami-Ono ~100 (commercial-mixed at the station front), Higashi-Rinkan ~95 (volatile series), Hashimoto ~90 — adjusted UP, because the raw station figure (~46) is dragged down by urbanisation-control and very large lots; the commercial station frontage is excluded — Sagamihara ~80, Yabe ~80 (thin official series), Fuchinobe ~75 (adjusted up for large-lot drag in the raw figures), Kobuchi ~75, Odakyu-Sagamihara ~70, Sobudai-mae ~60, Aihara ~55 (thin), Minami-Hashimoto ~55 (thin, conflicting sources), Kamimizo ~50 (mixed catchment — Tana-side lots score in the ¥30s), Tamazakai ~50 (thin, indicative), Banda ~42 (thin), Shimomizo ~36 and Harataima ~35 (thin, rural fringe). Sagamiko (~10) and Fujino (~11) are a different, rural market and no listing there is scored against urban figures. Aggregator district prints of ¥200–253万/tsubo in Midori ward and around Sagami-Ono were composition artefacts and are rejected, as is a 2026 year-to-date Midori land print of −20% resting on 5 deals. Walk bands apply the urban corridor's observed gradient — land falls ~20–25% by a 10–15-minute walk on official points; the city-wide band figure (−47%) is fringe-contaminated and is not applied in-corridor. Used houses transacted at about ¥112万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Minami ward ~125, Chuo ward ~111, Midori ward ~94 on a mixed catchment; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~137 falls to ~73 for 30+-yr stock, which is land-value territory. Official residential land prices rose in all three wards in the 2026 公示地価 survey: Chuo +5.1%, Minami +4.5%, Midori +3.2% — fastest at Hashimoto and Sagami-Ono, flat in the rural west.
